source: Published MySEQ offset list, labeled PatchDate=09/16/2026. Client hash in the pasted list had a line-wrap space in it ('...7751ae 6') that isn't in the real 40-char sha1 -- matches eqoffsets.buildinfo.client_hash() on the binary exactly once closed up. Same situation as known/2026-08-19.json: the binary was compiled 09/11/2026 but the list wasn't published/labeled until later.

_provenance.method: cli.py resolve --binary binaries/2026-09-11/eqgame.exe --sigs sigs/2026-08-19.json --known known/2026-08-19.json, run cold (no known-offsets for this patch yet), then checked field-by-field against this published list once it arrived.

comparison_2026_09_16.memory_offsets: all 6 matched exactly, including all 3 that had a SPLIT vote at resolve time (ZoneAddr 4/5, CharInfo 2/5, TargetAddr 2/3) -- majority-vote-with-partial-signature-survival was correct again, same as the 08/19 boundary.
comparison_2026_09_16.struct_offsets: 29 of 31 auto-confirmed and all correct. 2 were left UNCONFIRMED by resolve's consistency check (LevelOffset, HideOffset) rather than auto-applied -- see 'unconfirmed_fields' below for what the raw votes looked like and whether the plurality would have been right.

unconfirmed_fields.LevelOffset: 0x210 -> 0x270 (published). resolve's raw votes were 0x270 x4, 0x210(stale) x3, 0x352 x1 -- the plurality (0x270) was actually correct, but 3 dissenting votes meant Resolution.consistent was false, so resolve correctly declined to auto-apply it and carried the stale 0x210 forward as UNCONFIRMED instead.
unconfirmed_fields.HideOffset: 0x304 -> 0x504 (published). resolve's raw votes were 0x314 x2, 0x504 x1 -- here the PLURALITY WAS WRONG. The one signature that voted 0x504 (HideOffset#8) was correct and got outvoted by two signatures that had drifted onto something else. This is exactly the scenario Resolution.consistent exists for: had resolve.py used a bare plurality instead of requiring no dissent, this patch would have shipped a wrong HideOffset -- the same failure mode as the original manual HideOffset mistake this project's anchoring was built to prevent, this time caught by the tool refusing to guess instead of by a published list.
